title: Universal nodal relative-dimension-one locus for algebraic spaces
statement: Algebraic spaces are as in [def-trf-algebraic-space], with the universe convention [def-weil-size-convention]. Flatness and local finite presentation for their morphisms are tested on etale scheme charts using [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. A morphism of algebraic spaces is proper if it is separated, of finite type and universally closed: separated means its diagonal is a closed immersion, finite type means quasi-compact and locally of finite type on etale charts, and universally closed means closed on underlying spaces after every algebraic-space base change (the scheme conventions are [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]). Let $f:X\to Y$ be flat and locally of finite presentation. There is a largest open subspace $V\subseteq X$ on which $f$ is at-worst-nodal of relative dimension one, and formation of $V$ commutes with every base change $Y'\to Y$. More precisely, on any geometric fibre over an algebraically closed field $\Omega$ [def-weil-geometric-fibre, def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], the inverse image $V_\Omega$ consists exactly of the points with a neighbourhood smooth of relative dimension one [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] and the ordinary nodes. An ordinary node is a closed point whose completed local ring is $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$ [def-weil-closed-points, def-weil-pbc-adic-completion, def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. The topology and fibre conditions for algebraic spaces are tested on etale scheme charts; no equidimensionality assumption is imposed on the whole of $X$ or on its fibres.

source.place: Tag 0DSH (lemma-locus-where-nodal), with lemma-nodal-local and definition-nodal-family; fibrewise meaning from curves.tex lemma-locus-where-nodal.

proof.text: First handle an arbitrary flat locally finitely presented scheme morphism $h:U\to T$, without a fibre-dimension hypothesis. Put $L=L_1(h)$ from [lem-sfb-syntomic-fixed-dimension-locus]. Its restriction is flat and locally of finite presentation, and all nonempty geometric fibres are pure of dimension one. Apply [lem-trf-nodal-open-locus] to $h|_L$ and denote its nodal open by $N\subseteq L\subseteq U$. The cited statement applies because the purity hypothesis has now been verified on $L$, rather than assumed on $U$. Both $L$ and $N$ are open in $U$.

source.place: Tag 0DSH, reduction to the scheme case; curves.tex Tag 0DSC, restriction to the syntomic relative-dimension-one piece.

proof.text: This $N$ is the largest nodal source open for $h$. Indeed, let $O\subseteq U$ be any open on which $h$ is nodal. Each geometric fibre $O_\Omega$ is pure one-dimensional and its closed points are smooth or nodes. Apply [lem-trf-nodal-curve-lci-criterion], implication (1) to (2), to that fibre (taking its first-Fitting singular subscheme): the fibre is a local complete intersection. Thus $h|_O$ is syntomic by the explicit geometric-fibre definition in [lem-sfb-syntomic-fixed-dimension-locus], and its fibres are pure one-dimensional. Largestness in that node gives $O\subseteq L$. Now [lem-trf-nodal-open-locus] on $L$ gives $O\subseteq N$. For every scheme base change $T'\to T$, the first cited node identifies $L_1(h_{T'})$ with $L\times_TT'$, and the second identifies its nodal open with $N\times_TT'$. The same construction therefore proves arbitrary scheme base-change compatibility, without any purity assumption on $h$.

source.place: Tag 0DSH, scheme-locus input, with curves.tex Tag 0DSC and Tag 0C4E.

proof.text: Record the precise fibrewise meaning of this scheme locus. Let $C=U_\Omega$. A point with a smooth relative-dimension-one neighbourhood belongs to $L_1(h)_\Omega$ by [lem-sfb-syntomic-fixed-dimension-locus]. So does every ordinary node $c$: its completion is $A=\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-field-cohen-regular-complete] the power series ring is a local domain; hence the nonzero nonunit $uv$ is a regular sequence of length one. Also $\dim A=1$: a prime containing $uv$ contains $u$ or $v$, and the corresponding quotients are the one-variable power series domains of dimension one furnished by the same node. Every chain lies in one of these two branches, and the chain $(u)\subsetneq(u,v)$ has length one. The closed-point completed-ring criterion in [lem-sfb-syntomic-fixed-dimension-locus] now puts $c$ in $L_1(h)_\Omega$. Apply the fibrewise description of [lem-trf-nodal-open-locus] on $L_1(h)$: its $N_\Omega$ contains all these points and consists only of smooth curve points and nodes. Local rings and completions are unchanged by open restriction, so the pointwise description is in $C$, with no purity assumption on $C$.

source.place: Tag 0DSH, geometric-fibre interpretation from curves.tex Tag 0DSC; algebra.tex Tag 032C for the completed node.

proof.text: Choose a surjective etale scheme atlas $T\to Y$ and then a surjective etale scheme atlas $U\to X\times_YT$ using [def-trf-algebraic-space]. By [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] and the etale composition rule [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation], tested on scheme charts, their composite $p:U\to X$ is surjective etale. Write $h:U\to T$ for the top morphism. By the assumed chartwise flatness and local finite presentation, $h$ satisfies the hypotheses of Steps 1--3. Let $N\subseteq U$ be its scheme locus, and let $V\subseteq X$ be the image open subspace of $N\to X$. This exists by [lem-a1-space-etale-open-image], which also makes $N\to V$ surjective etale. The diagram $N\to T$ over $V\to Y$ has etale vertical arrows and a surjective source arrow. Since its top morphism is nodal, [lem-sfb-space-nodal-chart-locality] gives that $V\to Y$ is nodal.

source.place: Tag 0DSH, choice of charts and the open image; Tag 0DSG, condition (7).

proof.text: Let $O\subseteq X$ be any open subspace with $O\to Y$ nodal. Apply [lem-sfb-space-nodal-chart-locality] to the diagram $p^{-1}O\to T$ over $O\to Y$. It says that the top scheme morphism is nodal, so Step 2 gives $p^{-1}O\subseteq N$. Because $p$ is surjective, each point of $O$ lifts to $p^{-1}O$, and therefore lies in the image open $V$. Thus $O\subseteq V$ on points, and hence as open subspaces by [lem-a1-space-etale-open-image]. This proves largestness. Apply the same argument with $O=V$: it gives $p^{-1}V\subseteq N$, while the definition of the image gives $N\subseteq p^{-1}V$. Consequently $p^{-1}V=N$. The construction and this equality hold for any choice of charts; different choices give the same $V$ by largestness.

source.place: Tag 0DSH, nodal descent and largestness; the parenthetical inverse-image equality made explicit.

proof.text: Fix any algebraic-space morphism $Y'\to Y$. Set $X'=X\times_YY'$ and $T'=T\times_YY'$. Choose a surjective etale scheme atlas $Z\to T'$. Since $T'$ is a base change of the surjective etale atlas $T\to Y$, the composite $Z\to Y'$ is surjective etale. Put $U_Z=U\times_TZ$; here $U,T,Z$ are schemes, so this is a scheme. Associativity of fibre products identifies it with $(U\times_YY')\times_{T'}Z$. The covering and representability assertions of [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], together with the scheme etale composition rule [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation] on charts, show that $U_Z\to X'$ is a surjective etale scheme atlas. Thus $U_Z\to Z$ is an admissible chart diagram for $X'\to Y'$. It is the scheme base change of $h$, so is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change] and locally of finite presentation by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](3). This also verifies chartwise that $X'\to Y'$ is flat and locally of finite presentation.

source.place: Tag 0DSH, last sentence: scheme refinement of the pulled-back charts for an arbitrary algebraic-space base change.

proof.text: Let $V'\subseteq X'$ be the largest nodal open constructed for $X'\to Y'$. By Step 5 in the chart diagram of Step 6, its inverse image in $U_Z$ is the nodal scheme locus of $U_Z\to Z$. Step 2 identifies this locus with $N\times_TZ$. On the other hand, the inverse image of $V\times_YY'$ in $U_Z$ is also $N\times_TZ$: substitute $p^{-1}V=N$ from Step 5 into the cartesian diagram of Step 6. The atlas $U_Z\to X'$ is surjective, so the two open subsets of $|X'|$ with equal inverse image are equal. By the open-subspace correspondence of [lem-a1-space-etale-open-image] the two open subspaces are equal. Hence $V'=V\times_YY'$ as required.

source.place: Tag 0DSH, last sentence: explicit comparison of the two source opens after a surjective scheme refinement.

proof.text: Finally base change to any geometric point $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$. Step 7 identifies the inverse image $V_\Omega$ with the largest nodal open for $X_\Omega\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$. Choose any surjective etale scheme atlas $A\to X_\Omega$ and use the target chart $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ itself. Step 5 identifies the inverse image of $V_\Omega$ with the scheme locus of $A\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$. By Step 3 this is precisely the smooth-relative-dimension-one points and ordinary nodes of $A$. The pointwise preservation and reflection assertion of [lem-sfb-space-nodal-chart-locality] identifies this condition with the same condition on $X_\Omega$, tested on these charts. Since the atlas is surjective, this proves the claimed equality of fibre subsets. Neither the construction nor this test has assumed pure dimension for the other components of any fibre.
